claim: The ArrayExpress functional-genomics data collection in BioStudies is an external EMBL-EBI resource storing high-throughput functional-genomics experiment metadata, processed data, raw data links, and reusable study records.

BioStudies is an external EMBL-EBI database that holds descriptions of biological studies, links to data in EMBL-EBI and external databases, and orphan/supplementary data that do not fit structured archives.
ClinicalTrials.gov is an external website and online database of clinical research studies and information about their results.
DailyMed is an external National Library of Medicine resource providing searchable current labeling submitted to FDA for prescription and nonprescription products.
DISGENET is an external platform for gene-disease and disease-genomics knowledge, including NLP-supported disease genomics data and gene-disease associations.
Dryad is an external nonprofit data repository committed to making research data available for reuse and preservation.

The European Genome-phenome Archive is an external service for permanent archiving and sharing of personally identifiable genetic, phenotypic, and clinical biomedical research data under controlled access.
The European Medicines Agency medicines portal is an external resource for information on centrally authorised human and veterinary medicines and related medicine data.
The European Nucleotide Archive is an external resource providing a comprehensive record of nucleotide sequencing information, including raw sequencing data.
Europe PMC is an external free life-sciences literature search resource providing access to trusted literature sources, including abstracts and full text where available.
FDALabel is an external FDA resource for full-text search across human prescription, biological, over-the-counter, and other drug labeling documents.
Figshare is an external research repository infrastructure provider for sharing, showcasing, and managing research outputs in discoverable and citable forms.

NCBI GEO is an external public functional-genomics repository supporting MIAME-compliant array and sequence-based submissions, with tools to query and download experiments and gene-expression profiles.
The NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog is an externally curated collection of human genome-wide association studies and association results that includes MS-relevant trait pages and downloadable GWAS resources.

The International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium is an external collaborative network producing MS genetics publications and resources; some outputs are open publications while some underlying genotype datasets use controlled access routes.

source_label: MS Society UK Types of MS page
claim: The MS Society UK Types of MS page is an external public reference resource for MS disease-course categories and patient-facing explanation.
MSBase is an international online registry and platform for neurologists studying MS and other neuro-immunological diseases, focused on collaborative real-world outcomes research.

The MS Data Alliance Catalogue is an external metadata catalogue for discovering real-world MS data sources; it lists metadata/descriptive data rather than exposing the underlying real-world datasets.
MSGD is an externally curated Multiple Sclerosis Gene Database cataloging MS-related gene knowledge across variants, RNA, protein, knockout, drug-target, and high-throughput entry types.
The MS International Federation Atlas of MS is an external public resource for MS epidemiology and global access-to-care statistics and downloadable country-level datasets.
NARCOMS is an MS registry centered on maintaining a database of individuals' MS experiences and making that information available for research through its consortium processes.

source_label: National MS Society disease modification page
claim: The National Multiple Sclerosis Society disease-modification page is an external public reference resource for MS disease-modifying therapy context.

source_label: National MS Society Types of MS page
claim: The National Multiple Sclerosis Society Types of MS page is an external public reference resource for MS clinical-course categories and patient/professional education context.

source_label: NHS England MS DMT treatment algorithm PDF
claim: The NHS England treatment algorithm for multiple sclerosis disease-modifying therapies is an external public framework for DMT decision-making in England.
NICE guideline NG220 is an external public clinical guideline resource covering diagnosis and management of multiple sclerosis in adults.
The NINDS Multiple Sclerosis Common Data Elements page is an external public resource for MS clinical-study data standards, CRF modules, and recommended data elements.

Open Targets Platform is an external data-integration tool for systematic therapeutic target identification and prioritization, including target-disease association evidence and downloadable platform data.
OSF is an external free/open-source research project management and sharing platform that supports private collaboration and public dissemination across the research lifecycle.
PubMed is an external free search and retrieval resource for biomedical and life-sciences literature citations and abstracts, with links to full text where available.
NCBI SRA is an external public repository for high-throughput sequencing data that stores raw sequencing data and alignment information to support reproducibility and reanalysis.
Zenodo is an external multidisciplinary open research repository hosted by CERN/OpenAIRE for preserving and sharing publications, data, software, and other research outputs.
NCBI Gene/RefSeq describes CD74 as an MHC class II-associated chaperone involved in antigen presentation and as a cell-surface receptor for macrophage migration inhibitory factor.

source_label: GWAS Catalog chr1 rs7522462 MS association row
claim: GWAS Catalog association row 23727 lists rs7522462-G at chr1q32.1 as a multiple-sclerosis risk allele with OR 1.11 and p-value 2e-9; the row reports C1orf106 and KIF21B as author genes and the SNP's genomic context includes GPR25 in the local interval.

source_label: PANTS Crohn anti-TNF blood immune-module response study
claim: A PANTS Crohn disease anti-TNF blood transcriptome study reported baseline immune gene-module differences associated with primary anti-TNF response and noted interferon-related genes upregulated uniquely in responders, while also reporting that baseline expression differences did not predict response with sufficient sensitivity for clinical use.

source_label: Diebold 2022 high-dimensional DMF immune-response monitoring study
claim: Diebold et al. reported high-dimensional immune profiling of PBMCs from dimethyl fumarate-treated MS patients and proposed a treatment-response monitoring population involving GM-CSF, IFN-gamma, and CXCR3-expressing memory T helper cells.

source_label: Montes Diaz 2018 DMF immune-cell composition study
claim: Montes Diaz et al. reported that dimethyl fumarate treatment in MS is associated with persistent changes in innate and adaptive immune-cell composition.

Goldman et al. studied patient-specific modulation of leukocyte response during dimethyl fumarate treatment in MS, including absolute lymphocyte count, absolute neutrophil count, and neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio.

source_label: Carlström 2019 DMF monocyte ROS response study
claim: Carlström et al. reported in a longitudinal RRMS dimethyl fumarate cohort that monocyte-related changes, including monocyte counts and monocytic ROS, distinguished beneficial treatment responders from non-responders.

source_label: Gafson 2018 DMF PBMC RNA-seq / NEDA-4 response study
claim: Gafson et al. studied PBMC RNA-seq in relapsing-remitting MS patients starting dimethyl fumarate, with baseline, 6-week, and 15-month samples and NEDA-4 response labels; early responder-associated transcriptome changes were reported at 6 weeks.

source_label: Sánchez-Sanz 2023 DMF PBMC response transcriptome / GSE235357
claim: Sánchez-Sanz et al. reported that dimethyl fumarate-treated MS responders and non-responders showed different PBMC transcriptomic responses during treatment, with GEO dataset GSE235357 listed for the transcriptomic profile.
A Multiple Sclerosis Journal study reported that DMF treatment response was associated with lymphocyte-subset changes, including disproportionate CD8+ T-cell reduction and altered CD4/CD8 ratio.
DailyMed labeling for dimethyl fumarate states that its therapeutic mechanism in MS is unknown while DMF and monomethyl fumarate have been shown to activate the Nrf2 pathway.
DailyMed labeling for natalizumab states that natalizumab binds the alpha-4 subunit of alpha-4 integrins and inhibits alpha-4-mediated leukocyte adhesion.
DailyMed labeling for ocrelizumab describes it as a CD20-directed cytolytic antibody for relapsing and primary progressive MS, with a presumed mechanism involving binding CD20 on B lymphocytes.

source_label: bioRxiv EBV anti-CNS B-cell APC preprint
claim: A 2026 bioRxiv preprint reports that EBV can reprogram autoreactive anti-CNS B cells as antigen-presenting cells in MS.
A Nature study reported clonally expanded B cells in MS that bind EBV EBNA1 and GlialCAM, supporting EBV-linked B-cell molecular mimicry context in MS.
A longitudinal military cohort study reported a strong association between EBV infection and subsequent MS risk.

A sponsor phase 3 presentation reported that fenebrutinib met the prespecified non-inferiority criterion versus ocrelizumab for 12-week composite confirmed disability progression in primary progressive multiple sclerosis (hazard ratio 0.88, 95% CI 0.75 to 1.03), with a favorable timed 9-hole peg test component; full peer-reviewed reporting was pending at access time.

The FENtrepid PPMS registry record states that qualified researchers may request participant-level clinical data under Roche's data-sharing process and lists an active ocrelizumab comparator, composite disability progression, MRI, safety, pharmacokinetics, and blood NfL endpoints; the study remained active and not recruiting at access time.
IUPHAR/Guide to Pharmacology lists GPR25 as a Class A orphan GPCR with emerging pharmacology.

source_label: Nature Communications MS-IBD shared genetics GPR25 context
claim: External MS-IBD shared-genetics literature includes GPR25 among putative functional genes in shared or cross-disease genetic analyses.

The HERCULES ClinicalTrials.gov record states that qualified researchers may request anonymized participant-level data and related study documents through Vivli, subject to Sanofi's review and data-sharing conditions.

source_label: HERCULES public endpoint inventory and statistical analysis plan
claim: The public HERCULES registry and statistical analysis plan list plasma neurofilament light, serum CHI3L1, immunoglobulins, a lymphocyte-phenotyping subset of up to 200 participants, pharmacokinetic samples, serial disability measures, and MRI outcomes; availability and timepoint completeness in a shared participant-level package remain to be verified.
A Journal of Immunology EAE study reported that HLA-DRA1 constructs blocked CD74 expression and MIF effects in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.

A human microglia GPCR study reported functional CXCR4 expression, higher expression in white- than grey-matter microglia, and modest enrichment in MS lesional microglia; parts of its transcriptomic analysis reuse public datasets including the GSE111972 lineage.

source_label: Frontiers in Immunology UC colonoid tofacitinib MHC-II study
claim: A UC colonoid study reports that tofacitinib reduced TNF and poly(I:C)-induced STAT1 activation and MHC-II expression in colonic epithelial organoids.

source_label: Nature Immunology longitudinal anti-TNF single-cell atlas
claim: A Nature Immunology study reported a longitudinal single-cell atlas of anti-TNF treatment across immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, providing cross-disease cellular treatment-response context.

A Journal of Medical Genetics letter reported replication of KIF21B as a susceptibility locus for multiple sclerosis and noted prior establishment of KIF21B as a susceptibility locus for inflammatory bowel disease and MS.

source_label: Active intervention design in causal models
claim: A published active-learning framework selected interventions to reduce uncertainty in causal models, providing an external computational precedent for choosing informative perturbations rather than screening every intervention uniformly.

Compressed Perturb-seq was reported to use composite perturbation measurements and sparse recovery to reduce experimental cost while retaining single-perturbation and second-order interaction information in a human macrophage model.

A published platform used inducible CRISPR interference and activation in human iPSC-derived microglia, including pooled screens and a single-cell transcriptomic readout, establishing an external technical precedent for bidirectional perturbation in a human microglial model.

source_label: In vivo CRISPR screen in neuroinflammation
claim: An in vivo CRISPR screening pipeline in mouse neuroinflammation was reported to perturb cytokine receptors and signaling molecules in editable progenitor-derived CNS myeloid populations with single-cell and functional readouts.
External prediction-model guidance and risk-of-bias tools emphasize prespecified evaluation, validation, applicability, and overfitting risk when developing or validating clinical prediction models.
Spatial Perturb-Seq was reported to jointly recover CRISPR perturbation identity, whole-transcriptome state, spatial location, and microenvironmental effects in intact mouse brain tissue.

source_label: Annual Reviews drug-target genetics and Open Targets context
claim: External target-prioritization literature emphasizes combining target-disease association evidence with tractability, safety, mechanism, and direction-of-effect information when building therapeutic hypotheses.

source_label: PLOS Genetics MS MHC fine-mapping study
claim: External MS MHC fine-mapping literature reports multiple statistically independent HLA and non-HLA effects within the MHC region.

source_label: EJI MIF/CD74 pathway in human B cells and MS
claim: A European Journal of Immunology study reported that MIF and the MIF receptor CD74 were downregulated, while CXCR4 was upregulated, in B cells from early MS patients, and described reciprocal regulation among MIF, CD74, and CXCR4 in human B cells.

source_label: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives MS biomarker review
claim: External MS biomarker reviews describe MS as heterogeneous and caution that a single marker may be insufficient for a complex disease.

source_label: MS Society UK Types of MS page
claim: Public MS clinical-reference sources describe primary progressive MS as a course with progression from the first symptoms rather than discrete relapse-remission attacks.

source_label: National MS Society Types of MS page
claim: Public MS clinical-reference sources describe relapsing-remitting MS as a disease course with distinct attacks followed by partial or complete recovery, and as the most common MS disease course.

source_label: National MS Society secondary progressive MS page
claim: Public MS clinical-reference sources describe secondary progressive MS as a progressive course that follows an initial relapsing-remitting course in many patients.

source_label: Nature Communications MS-IBD shared genetics study
claim: External MS-IBD literature reports that treatment choices for one disease can have adverse or non-transferable effects in the other, including cautions around interferon-beta and TNF-alpha antagonist contexts.

source_label: Moll 2009 CXCR4/CXCL12 histopathology in chronic MS
claim: A human chronic-MS imaging and histopathology study reported CXCR4 and phospho-CXCR4 on reactive microglia/macrophages in active or chronic-active lesions, including MHC-II/CXCR4 double-positive cells.

source_label: van der Poel 2019 GSE111972 source publication
claim: The publication that generated GSE111972 reported CXCR4 among regionally differential and MS-associated genes in human microglia, including high expression in MS normal-appearing grey matter; it did not report the project's exact patient-equal CD44-plus-CXCR4 score or its broad-state adjustment.

A human progressive-MS active-lesion CyTOF study reported higher CD44 together with HLA-DR, CD45, CD68 and other inflammatory or phagocytic markers in lesion-enriched activated microglial clusters relative to homeostatic microglia.

source_label: Nature Communications MS-IBD shared genetics study
claim: A Nature Communications cross-trait GWAS study reported that the genetic correlation between multiple sclerosis and ulcerative colitis was greater than the genetic correlation between multiple sclerosis and Crohn disease in the datasets it analyzed.

The completed PERSEUS PPMS registry record states that qualified researchers may request anonymized participant-level data and related documents through Vivli and lists placebo-controlled disability, MRI, NfL, CHI3L1, immunoglobulin, lymphocyte-subset, pharmacokinetic, and safety endpoints; results and actual shared-field completeness were not posted in the registry at access time.

source_label: PLOS Genetics PTGER4 Crohn expression-modulation study
claim: A PLOS Genetics Crohn disease study mapped a 5p13.1 susceptibility region to a gene desert and reported modulation of PTGER4 expression as a plausible mechanism for the Crohn signal.

source_label: GWAS Catalog PTGER4 rs4613763 MS/Crohn association rows
claim: GWAS Catalog rs4613763 association rows preserve a PTGER4 disease-pair allele contrast: the Crohn disease row lists rs4613763-C as the risk allele with OR 1.32, while the multiple-sclerosis row lists rs4613763-G as the risk allele with OR 1.20.

source_label: Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases RA/SLE pregnancy single-cell transcriptome study
claim: External longitudinal single-cell blood-transcriptome work profiles pregnancy trajectories in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and healthy controls.

source_label: Sanofi member page on the Vivli platform
claim: Sanofi's Vivli member policy says researchers may use the Vivli Enquiry Form for Sanofi studies not listed on the platform and may enquire about study documents without participant-level data. Its ordinary data-sharing feasibility criteria include study completion and public or accepted primary results, plus absence of regulatory, legal, privacy, and technical constraints. Therefore an ongoing NCT06372145 ToleDYNAMIC package with no posted results should be approached first as an availability/document enquiry or sponsor scientific-collaboration request, not assumed eligible for immediate standard IPD release.

The phase 3 MS-STAT2 trial reported no reduction in 6-month confirmed disability progression with simvastatin versus placebo in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (40% versus 36%; hazard ratio 1.13, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.39).
Bagnoud et al. analyzed whole-blood transcriptomes in MS relapse and reported genes associated with glucocorticoid-sensitive versus glucocorticoid-resistant response.
Hecker et al. profiled CD19+ B-cell and CD4+ T-cell transcriptomes before and after high-dose methylprednisolone therapy for MS relapse, providing cell-type-specific glucocorticoid-response context.
Airla et al. reported peripheral blood immune-system gene suppression after methylprednisolone treatment during multiple sclerosis exacerbations.

The European Commission authorized tolebrutinib (Cenrifki) in June 2026 for adults with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis without relapses in the preceding two years; the European product information includes liver-risk precautions and monitoring.

source_label: FDA Complete Response Letter for NDA 219624
claim: The US Food and Drug Administration issued a Complete Response Letter for tolebrutinib in December 2025, stating that severe potentially fatal drug-induced liver injury prevented a favorable benefit-risk conclusion and that the proposed mitigation did not adequately address the risk.

source_label: FDA HERCULES subgroup and benefit-risk assessment
claim: In its review of HERCULES, the US Food and Drug Administration reported substantially larger subgroup treatment-effect estimates among participants with baseline gadolinium-enhancing lesions and among treatment-naive participants than among participants without enhancing lesions or with multiple prior therapies; it concluded that the population with a favorable benefit-risk profile was not clinically established. Baseline gadolinium activity and prior-therapy count were listed as subgroup factors in the final public statistical analysis plan, while the broader active-versus-non-active interpretation remained limited by missing historical MRI.

The phase 3 HERCULES trial reported that tolebrutinib reduced 6-month confirmed disability progression versus placebo in non-relapsing secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (22.6% versus 30.7%; hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.55 to 0.88), while liver-enzyme elevations were more frequent with tolebrutinib.

Sanofi reported that the phase 3 PERSEUS trial of tolebrutinib in primary progressive multiple sclerosis did not meet its primary endpoint of delaying 6-month composite confirmed disability progression.

The public HERCULES protocol describes ToleDYNAMIC, an 80-participant immunological substudy spanning HERCULES and PERSEUS (about 40 participants from each) with samples at baseline, month 3, and month 12; it repeatedly specifies tolebrutinib-treated participants and sampling after initiation of tolebrutinib, so the public design supports an active-treatment-only interpretation unless sponsor metadata establish otherwise. Planned measurements include B-cell and CD14-monocyte RNA sequencing in a subset, detailed lymphocyte/monocyte phenotyping, CD64 and other monocyte-state markers, cytokines, myelin phagocytosis, reactive oxygen species, and Seahorse metabolic assays linked to parent-trial clinical and MRI data.

source_label: Official ClinicalTrials.gov registry record and API v2 JSON
claim: The official NCT06372145 registry record names ToleDYNAMIC as a biomarker substudy in an active, nonrandomized, open-label phase 3 extension. It states that participants from the progressive-MS parent trials start open-label tolebrutinib, lists biomarker change from extension baseline through 12 months, reports no posted results, and estimates study completion in April 2029. The record permits qualified-researcher IPD requests through Vivli but does not establish that ongoing ToleDYNAMIC assay data are currently shareable.

source_label: HMG autoimmune GWAS loci expression study with ZMIZ1 context
claim: A Human Molecular Genetics study of autoimmune GWAS loci in immune cells reported rs1250551 as an MS-associated ZMIZ1 locus with mononuclear-phagocyte and vitamin-D-context expression effects.

source_label: GWAS Catalog ZMIZ1 rs1250550 MS/Crohn association rows
claim: GWAS Catalog rs1250550 association rows preserve a disease-specific allele-direction contrast at ZMIZ1: the multiple-sclerosis row lists rs1250550-A as the risk allele with OR 1.10, while a Crohn disease row lists rs1250550-G as the risk allele with OR 1.19.
